newsitem.title: UK: Lonrho shares shrug off hotel sale reports.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho shares shrug off hotel sale reports.

text.p: Reports suggesting Lonrho was exploring new ways to complete its break-up failed to excite investors, who have seen the conglomerate change course several times before as it tries to streamline its operations.
Shares in Lonrho were unchanged at 147-1/2 pence in mid-afternoon, after newspapers reported Lonrho looks unlikely to be able to sell its Princess hotel chain in one go.
Analysts said the hotel sale is a necessary step before Lonrho can finally hive off its African trading operations from its mining rump.

But they hoped the group's split-up, set out over a year go, will gain extra momentum after Lonrho on Friday announced the appointment of John Craven, the former British ambassador to South Africa, as its chairman.
Craven, who is the non-executive chairman of investment bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, should have the contacts and the skills to complete Lonrho's demerger, industry watchers said.
"He has the deal-making abilities and the contacts in South Africa and Europe that Lonrho needs," said Charles Kernot at Paribas Capital Markets.

Craven, who will succeed Sir John Leahy, may fill the void left by German businesman Dieter Bock, who initiated Lonrho's demerger process before stepping down as non-executive director last week to return to the real estate business.

Lonrho initially wanted to demerge its mining operations, then decided to demerge its hotels activities instead only to eventually opt for an outright sale. This divestment would then likely be followed by a demerger of the trading operations, Lonrho said two months ago.
But so far, Lonrho only realised the 327 million pound sale of its Metropole hotels to Glasgow-based Stakis Plc in September.
The Financial Times reported Lonrho is now considering to split the Princess hotel chain, while the conglomerate is also said mulling the sale of its African sugar interests.

South African-listed Lonrho Sugar Ltd, in which British Lonrho has a 94 percent stake, said late last month it was holding share-price sensitive talks with third parties, prompting market talk of a takeover.
Lonrho, in which South Africa's Anglo American has a 28 percent stake, was earlier said to be talking to sell the the Princess hotel chain to Saudi Prince al-Waleed bin Talal.
But newspapers now say the Prince is only interested in buying part of the chain, which has hotels in the U.S, Mexico and the Caribbean region.
No-one was immediately available at Lonrho to comment.
